## 19.Reporting and escalation

## 19.1 Escalation principles

resolved. An owner who believes a risk is under control must still escalate it if it meets the threshold. Escalation is mandatory, not discretionary. The threshold is the assessed rating of the risk, not the confidence of the owner that it will be

EscalationLadder—Authorityand NamedEscalationContact 
Critical (20-25)BoardRiskCommittee A.Brightwell·+1（212）555-0108
High (13-19)Group Exec Risk Committee M.Achebe·+1（212）555-0147
Elevated (8-12)Divisional Risk Committee D.Kulkarni·+918045550182
Moderate (4-7)Business Unit Head S.Marchetti-Lang·+1(212)555-0174
Low (1-3)Control Owner N.Osadebe·+1(646)555-0188

Figure 12 — Escalation ladder, decision authority and the named escalation contact at each level.

## 19.2 Immediate escalation triggers

The following must be escalated to the Group CRO immediately on identification (M. T. Achebe, +1 212 555-0147, mobile +1 917 555-0143), irrespective of scheduled reporting cycles:

* Any risk assessed eis Critical, or any breach of a Board-level appetite limit.

* Any occurrence in a zero-appetite category, or any Severity 1 incident.

* Any suspected material regulatory breach or unplanned regulatory contact regarding a potential breach.

•Any confirmed or suspected personal data breach.

•Any suspected fraud involving anemployee,or external fraudabove theGroupreporting threshold.

•Any circumstance reasonably expected to attract significant adverse media attention.

•Any inability to meet an impact tolerance for an important business service.

19.3 Reporting calendar and distribution

| REPORT | FREQUENCY | PREPAREDBY | DISTRIBUTION |
|---|---|---|---|
| Group Risk ProfileReport | Quarterly | Tobias Lindgvist (t.lindgvist@cadencefg.com) | brc@cadencefg.com:board@cadencefq.com |
| ExecutiveRisk Dashboard | Monthly | Privanka S.Raghavan (p.raghavan@cadencefg.com) | gerc@cadencefg.com |
| Appetite Adherence Report | Monthly | Priyanka S.Raghavan | gerc@cadencefg.com; brc@cadencefg.com (quarterly) |
| IssueandRemediationReport | Monthly | Tobias Lindgvist | gerc@cadencefg.com |
| Incident andLossReport | Monthly | RafaelE.Duarte (r.duarte@cadencefg.com) | orc@cadencefg.com |
| EmergingRiskReport | Quarterly | Tobias Lindqvist | gerc@cadencefg.com;brc@cadencefg.com |
| RiskCultureReport | Annual | DelphineR.Okonjo (d.okonjo@cadencefg.com) | brc@cadencefg.com;remco@cadencefg.com |
| Framework Effectiveness Review | Annual | Miriam T.Achebe (m.achebe@cadencefg.com) | brc@cadencefg.com:board@cadencefg.com |
| Risk ConductReport | Annual | Miriam T.Achebe | remco@cadencefg.com (D.N.Quarshie) |

## 19.4Reportingstandards

* Reports state the position, the movement since the previous period and the forward outlook, not the position alone.

* Deteriorating positions are highlighted explicitly rather than left for the reader to infer.

•Data is reconciledto source,with the source and as-at datestated oneverymaterialfigure.

•Estimates and manual adjustments are identified as such,with theirbasis disclosed.

• Where information is incomplete, the gap is disclosed rather than omitted.

•Reports are circulatedat leastfivebusiness days before the meeting atwhichthey are considered.

Aggregation capability. In linewith BCBS239,theGroup must be able to produceaccurate aggregatedrisk data rapidly,including ad hoc during a stress. Theabilityto meet ad-hocrequests within defined timeframes is tested at leastannuallyand results reported to the BoardRiskCommittee.
